title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
summary:
arXiv:2611.14681v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Today's AI workloads are rapidly changing: new models are released more often, model architectures are increasingly diverse, and traffic distributions change frequently. The challenge we face at Together AI is continual optimization for these changing workloads. Compiling a deployment into an optimized forward pass is a challenge that is well-suited for agent hill-climbing. Existing systems struggle with continual compilation due to a tradeoff between measurement throughput and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). On the other hand, systems use agents to directly optimize end-to-end engines but suffer from slow engine launch times. To address these challenges, we build Together Compiler (TKCC), the first truly continual agent loop designed for AI inference optimization. To address the throughput-fidelity tradeoff, we propose: (1) a Tiered Persistent Engine that decouples engine launch overheads from forward pass computation; (2) a cost model to select the parallelism configurations that seed the optimization process. We also conduct extensive ablations on agent context management and present our insights on deploying TKCC in production. TKCC outperforms highly-optimized hand-written Megakernels on the Llama 1B workhorse workload by up to 1.7x and the best open source engines on the latest frontier models (Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, DeepSeek v4.1 Flash) across hardware platforms by up to 2.6x higher TPS on the InferenceX benchmark. TKCC also sets the state-of-the-art performance at batch size 1, with 1111 TPS on M3.1 Flash and 1205 TPS on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash. Finally, TKCC generalizes beyond frontier language model inference. TKCC serves trillions of tokens across our production fleet.

title: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents
summary:
arXiv:2611.14765v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Current benchmarks for LLM-driven data agents saturate quickly and cannot target specific capabilities. We present SynthCorp, a platform that creates customizable data estates and benchmarks by simulating how business events produce and modify corporate data over time. Each data estate combines relational databases, a document store, and a data catalog, paired with evaluation tasks and executable gold programs. First, given a scenario and target complexity dimensions, SynthCorp synthesizes reusable event types and compiles each into a program over predefined simulation primitives. Second, SynthCorp schedules event instances on a virtual calendar, interleaving routine and disruption events so that tables, documents, and catalog entries remain consistent. Third, SynthCorp executes the calendar to materialize the data estate and records every operation in a simulation log. Fourth, SynthCorp generates analytical tasks and derives verified gold programs from the log. We use SynthCorp to generate initial evaluation benchmarks comprising seven data estates (up to 1K operational tables) and 256 tasks across five domains. The data estates pass deterministic pipeline checks (such as foreign-key violations, undeclared writes, recurrence violations, and database execution failures) with a near-zero error rate, introduce cross-asset complexities, and cover all requested dimensions. Evaluating three models across four data-context settings shows that the benchmarks separate data contexts and model tiers. Auditing candidate queries against causal provenance in the simulation log verifies gold programs without manual annotation, including on multi-event composite tasks that expose reasoning failures in state-of-the-art agents. We hope the community uses SynthCorp to generate more challenging and useful data estates and benchmarks that foster the development of enterprise data agents.
title_es: SynthCorp: plataforma para benchmarks de agentes de datos
bajada: Investigadores presentan SynthCorp, plataforma que genera benchmarks personalizados simulando cómo eventos empresariales crean datos corporativos. Herramienta útil para evaluar agentes LLM en tareas de datos realistas.

title: The Fallout from Jensen’s Downfall
summary: Welcome, Weekenders!Jexit, as I’d like to christen Huang’s departure from Nvidia, is an ugly matter, an implosion with fallout across continents and several different industries. No one irradiated by it walks away a picture of good health.Huang obfuscated the truth,promising senior executives at his companythat he’d had just the one affair, with Alice Huang, the former executive at Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer. But that wasn’t the case. He reportedly had at least two others, including one with a direct report.Nvidia’s board almost didn’t act and only did so on the insistence of the company’s general counsel, Tim Teter. I’m not surprised. The boardis dominatedby people who’ve known Huang for decades. And there was not even a board chair.The friendships Huang thought he had in Washington weren’t nearly enough to save him, a reminder of the fickleness of politics as Silicon Valley goes through the necessary course correction to win influence with the ascendant left. (Alex Karp is a Democrat again, did youhear?) Indeed, it looks pretty obvious that some factions within Trump-led Washington worked against Huang. Many of the reporters who have been most active in the last week are in Washington.Some U.S. authorities say the former Megaspeed executive was a spy. Was she? Morereportsin recent days cast doubt on whether she really was. No matter. The mere implication was a useful weapon to wield against Huang.The spy-who-loved-him situation was catnip for reporters, but I don’t want to hand out laurels to the media. Huang’s bullying tendencies went underhighlighted for years—first because Nvidia was too complex and confusing to cover, and then because of Huang’s presentation of himself as a nerdish, articulate poster boy for the AI age. It makes me wonder who else is escaping close coverage as the tech landscape continues to widen and morph.Throughout Jexit, Huang has maintained a sizable base of support in Silicon Valley. title: ag-ui-protocol /ag-ui
summary:
AG-UI: The Agent-User Interaction Protocol AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.
Built for simplicity and flexibility, it enables seamless integration between AI agents, real time user context, and user interfaces. Join our Discord → Read the Docs → Go to the AG-UI Dojo → Follow us → 🚀 Getting Started Create a new AG-UI application in seconds: npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app Useful Links: The AG-UI Dojo Build AG-UI-powered applications(Quickstart) Build new AG-UI framework integrations (Quickstart) Book a call to discuss an AG-UI integration with a new framework Join the Discord Community What is AG-UI? AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed for simplicity & flexibility: During agent executions, agent backends emit events compatible with one of AG-UI's ~16 standard event types Agent backends can accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs as arguments AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer that ensures compatibility across diverse environments: Works with any event transport (SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.) Allows for loose event format matching , enabling broad agent and app interoperability It also ships with a reference HTTP implementation and default connector to help teams get started fast. Learn more about the specs → Why AG-UI? AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions. Where does AGUI fit in the agentic protocol stack? AG-UI is complementary to the other 2 top agentic protocols MCP gives agents tools A2A allows agents to communicate with other agents AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications 🚀 Features 💬 Real-time agentic chat with streaming 🔄 Bi-directional state synchronization 🧩 Generative UI and structured messages 🧠 Real-time context enrichment 🛠️ Frontend tool integration 🧑‍💻 Human-in-the-loop collaboration 🛠 Supported Integratio

The engine reads checkpoints, tokenizes requests and runs Metal or CUDA kernels directly.
Serving needs no Python or MLX installation. Building with a coding agent? Have it load the contributor skill before it writes any code. Contributing with agents Please use Agent Traffic Control before editing TensorFold so contributors and agents can avoid duplicate work and conflicting changes.
Check the live agent radar before choosing an issue and follow CONTRIBUTING.md and the ATC contributor instructions . Install or upgrade ATC to 0.9.4 or later, then run from an updated TensorFold clone: npm install -g github:ashhart/ATC
atc check ISSUE --json
atc claim ISSUE --json Replace ISSUE with the issue number and claim only after a complete check says the work is free.
TensorFold enables automatic public check-ins: a successful new claim starts an anonymous session on the radar and returns its session number.
Keep that number instead of starting a duplicate session.
For work already yours, start a session with atc start ISSUE --json .
Add --github-name to claim or start only if you want your verified GitHub name shown; --local keeps a new session on your machine.
The board shows the issue, activity state and last check-in; GitHub still associates the verification comment with its author.
Check that publication is public ; unavailable means the public update failed even if the local claim or session succeeded. Pulse only while the agent is working, before its five-minute check-in expires: atc pulse ISSUE SESSION working --json
atc who path/to/file --json
atc overlap --json
atc land ISSUE SESSION --json
atc release ISSUE --json Use reviewing or blocked when appropriate, land the session when it stops, and resolve overlaps before opening a pull request.
Before opening a pull request, have the agent run the pull request skill ; agents that support skills can install it as tensorfold-pul

bajada_en: TensorFold enables serving language models from Zig binaries on Apple Silicon and NVIDIA GPUs without Python. It optimizes direct execution of Metal or CUDA kernels for better performance.

summary: Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Start with open-source Sheets and Docs, then connect your own application or agent. 🚀 Quick start · 📚 Documentation · ⚖️ Feature comparison · 🌐 Website · 🎮 Showcase · 🔧 API Reference · 📝 Blog English · Français · Deutsch · Español · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 Table of contents 💡 What is Univer? Open-source capabilities 🚀 Build on the open-source foundation Quick start: an open-source spreadsheet editor Connect your application to editable content 🏗️ Explore the open-source architecture Give custom features clear boundaries Compose cross-feature edits and undo/redo Connect applications and agents through Facade APIs and events 🧩 Extend your application with Univer Office SDK Scope and licensing 🌐 Application patterns and ecosystem Univer Workspace: an Office SDK reference application CLI, agent integrations, and developer skills 📚 Documentation and contributing Runtime compatibility 💬 Community 🔒 Security ❤️ Sponsors 📄 License 💡 What is Univer? Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs. Univer Office SDK has three parts: Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor. Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export. AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations. This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementation
title_es: Univer: SDK open-source para construir Office con IA
bajada: Se lanzó Univer Office SDK, un framework open-source para construir aplicaciones de oficina con capacidades de hojas de cálculo, documentos y agentes IA integrados. Permite extender aplicaciones existentes sin bloqueo de proveedor.
bajada_en: Univer Office SDK launched, an open-source framework for building office applications with integrated spreadsheets, docs, and AI agents. Enables extending existing applications without vendor lock-in.
